claims.text: Inserting an ultrathin coherent B2-ordered interlayer into an HEA multilayer will shift the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep.
An Al-containing HEA such as AlCoCrFeNi can provide the proposed coherent B2-ordered interlayer.
The coherent B2 interlayer reduces atomic diffusivity at HEA interfaces.
The coherent B2 interlayer permits coherent dislocation transmission.
HEA multilayers with relatively incoherent interfaces primarily exhibit diffusion-mediated creep at elevated temperature.
Low stress exponents and low activation energies are expected for the proposed diffusion-mediated baseline behavior.
The proposed B2 interlayer has low lattice misfit relative to the adjoining HEA matrices.
At 500–600 °C, both diffusion and dislocation processes are active during creep.
A coherent B2 interlayer acts as a robust barrier to atomic diffusion while maintaining geometric continuity.
Lower local diffusion coefficients across the B2 interface suppress vacancy-driven diffusion creep.
Preservation of a continuous coherent lattice causes dislocations to accumulate and transmit stress.
Dislocation-mediated creep should exhibit higher stress exponents and activation energies than the proposed diffusion-mediated regime.
Adding the B2 interlayer will increase the measured stress exponent relative to an otherwise identical multilayer without the interlayer.
Adding the B2 interlayer will increase the measured creep activation energy relative to the control.
Adding the B2 interlayer will reduce the steady-state creep rate relative to the control.
Control multilayers without the engineered interlayer display lower stress exponents and higher creep rates under identical conditions.
The beneficial mechanism transition is limited to temperatures at which the B2 interlayer remains coherent and thermally stable, likely below approximately 700 °C.
Above approximately 700 °C, interlayer degradation or phase transformation may prevent the proposed creep-mechanism shift.
The magnitude of the creep-parameter shift depends on interlayer thickness, chemical composition, and processing conditions.
